checked_ok.claim: Expo SDK 57 is the current stable SDK on 2026-10-04: npm expo latest = 57.0.26; SDK 58 exists only under the next tag (58.0.3).
SDK 57 ships React Native 0.86 and React 19.2 (versions table: RN 0.86, React 19.2.3).

New Architecture only: 'SDK 55 and later run entirely on the New Architecture. The New Architecture is always enabled and cannot be disabled.' All Phase 1 phone libraries in the plan are Expo modules.
Expo Router is current and versioned with the SDK (expo-router latest 57.0.24).

A local native module needs a development build, not Expo Go: a development build 'is essentially your own version of Expo Go where you are free to use any native libraries and change any native configuration.'
npx create-expo-module@latest --local creates the module under ./modules, which Expo Autolinking searches by default ('nativeModulesDir ... defaults to ./modules/').
No config plugin is needed for the planned iOS privacy-manifest entry: it goes in app config under ios.privacyManifests.
SDK 57 minimums: Android 7+, iOS 16.4+ (compileSdk/targetSdk 36, Xcode 26.4+).
SDK 58 keeps the same minimums (row '| 58.0.0 | 7+ | 37 | 36 | 16.4+ | 26.4+ |'), so line 516 survives the SDK move.
StatCounter Turkey mobile, Sept 2026 CSV: Android below 7.0 = 6.0 1.49 + 5.1 0.17 + 5.0 0.07 + 4.4 0.07 + 4.1 0.02 = 1.82% (mobile+tablet 2.03%), so about 98% on Android 7+.
StatCounter Turkey mobile, Sept 2026 CSV: iOS below 16.4 = 2.30% (largest 15.8 at 1.48; mobile+tablet 2.41%), so about 97.5 to 97.7% on iOS 16.4+.
Zero: 'Zero does not support offline writes.' Writes are rejected while disconnected.
'Recently changed hands' is true for Electric: 'Electric is joining Databricks...' (2026-08-11); Electric Cloud is winding down.

A hand-written local queue drained with exponential backoff is the standard offline-first write pattern ('insert it into a queue. When the app gets back online, drain the queue with exponential backoff'); append-only data needs no sync engine.
Store on the phone first, send later, with the local store as the source of truth is the documented offline-first model.
TanStack Query 5 is still the current major (latest 5.104.1, modified 2026-10-02; no v6 tag).
@expo/app-integrity is still alpha ('This library is currently in alpha and will frequently experience breaking changes.'), so an exact version pin is right (npm latest 57.0.2).
expo-secure-store has this-device-only accessibility: WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY entries are 'not migrated to a new device when restoring from a backup'.
Expo's uptime call skips deep sleep on Android: getUptimeAsync 'Android devices do not count time spent in deep sleep.' Not using it is right.
On Apple platforms CLOCK_MONOTONIC 'will continue to increment while the system is asleep' (CLOCK_UPTIME_RAW does not).
Apple reason 35F9.1 matches the plan: boot-time data 'may not be sent off-device', except 'the amount of time that has elapsed between events that occurred within the app'.
expo-background-task is the current Expo background API; expo-background-fetch is deprecated (as of SDK 57) and replaced by it.
Android minimum 15 minutes and iOS timing chosen by BGTaskScheduler are as documented; Expo's Android worker also requires NetworkType.CONNECTED.

Batch upload with per-record results, resending only failed items with exponential backoff, matches DynamoDB BatchWriteItem (UnprocessedItems; 'we strongly recommend that you use an exponential backoff algorithm').

Capped exponential backoff plus jitter is the AWS pattern ('implementations typically cap their backoff', 'Jitter adds some amount of randomness'). The plan's Kaynaklar link aws.amazon.com/builders-library/... now 301-redirects here (republished 2026-06-12).
Retrying is safe because the phone-made record ID is the idempotency key (line 612): 'APIs with side effects aren't safe to retry unless they provide idempotency.'

expo-notifications (latest 57.0.21) does local-only notifications; scheduled ones are re-armed after reboot (RECEIVE_BOOT_COMPLETED added automatically); a non-exact daily reminder needs no SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM. No lighter maintained option: @notifee/react-native last published 2024-12-20.
One app for both roles fits Apple 4.3(a) ('Don't create multiple Bundle IDs of the same app'); size cost is small since both roles need camera and Bluetooth in later phases.

Delta pulls by server version with deletion markers follow Google's incremental sync model: 'the result will always contain deleted entries, so that the clients get the chance to remove them from storage.'

findings.plan_quote: TanStack Query 5 ve OpenAPI'den üretilen istemci.
findings.finding: With SQLite as the phone's source of truth, TanStack Query is a second cache on top of it. On React Native it also has to be wired to a network listener (onlineManager with expo-network or NetInfo) and to AppState (focusManager). The version is fine (5.104.1); the problem is that the phone does not need it. Student screens read SQLite; the few online-only instructor screens can call the generated openapi-fetch client directly.

evidence.quote: The local data source is the canonical source of truth for the app. It should be the exclusive source of any data that higher layers of the app read.
To add this behavior in React Native you have to use React Query onlineManager
latest: 5.104.1

Hoca modunun internet isteyen birkaç ekranı üretilen istemciyi doğrudan çağırır. TanStack Query yalnız web panelinde kalır; Teknolojiler özetindeki Telefon satırından da çıkarırım.

Expo documents a PRAGMA user_version migration pattern, and enableChangeListener plus addDatabaseChangeListener covers live screen updates. Dropping drizzle on the phone removes 3 packages and 2 build-config edits.

evidence.quote: npm i drizzle-orm@rc / npm i -D drizzle-kit@rc ... config.resolver.sourceExts.push('sql');
await db.execAsync(`PRAGMA user_version = ${DATABASE_VERSION}`);

findings.plan_quote: Yoklama verildiği anda, uygulama açılınca, internet gelince ve fırsat buldukça arka planda denenir.
findings.finding: No request timeout is defined. React Native's Android HTTP client is built with connect, read and write timeouts of 0 ('No timeouts by default'), so a send on a half-working campus network can hang and block the sequential queue. For the 'internet gelince' trigger, expo-network is already in the app (Better Auth's Expo install line includes it), but on iOS isInternetReachable just mirrors isConnected, so a captive portal looks online; only the request itself can tell.

evidence.quote: .connectTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) .writeTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS)
A best practice in Amazon is to set a timeout on any remote call, and generally on any call across processes even on the same box.
On iOS, this value will always be the same as `isConnected`.
npm install better-auth @better-auth/expo expo-secure-store expo-network

findings.recommendation_tr: Her gönderme ve indirme isteğine kendi zaman aşımımı koyarım (örneğin 30 saniye); süresi dolan istek iptal edilir ve normal yeniden deneme sırasına girer. Cevap beklenen biçimde değilse (kampüs ağının giriş sayfası gibi) gönderim başarısız sayılır. 'İnternet gelince' tetiği için zaten kurulu olan expo-network'ün dinleyicisini kullanırım; iPhone'da bu yalnız bağlantı olduğunu söyler, internete gerçekten çıkılıp çıkılmadığını gönderimin kendisi gösterir.

findings.plan_quote: Başarısız gönderim 2 saniyeden 10 dakikaya kadar artan, rastgele kaydırılmış aralıklarla yeniden denenir.
findings.finding: The server plans @fastify/under-pressure (503) and @fastify/rate-limit (429, retry-after header on by default). The phone's retry rule does not honour Retry-After, so at the class-exit peak phones may come back sooner than the server asked, which is exactly when the server is shedding load.

evidence.quote: The server MAY send a Retry-After header field (Section 10.2.3) to suggest an appropriate amount of time for the client to wait before retrying the request.
The response representations SHOULD include details explaining the condition, and MAY include a Retry-After header indicating how long to wait before making a new request.
You can configure the error message and the `Retry-After` header.

findings.recommendation_tr: Sunucu 503 ya da 429 ile 'şu kadar sonra dene' (Retry-After) derse telefon en az o kadar bekler; kendi hesapladığı bekleme süresiyle bu sürenin büyük olanını kullanır.

findings.plan_quote: İlk sürümlerde yazılım anahtarı (@noble/curves, expo-secure-store "yalnız bu cihaz") kabul edilir
findings.finding: Reinstall and restore do not behave as the plan assumes ('silip yeniden kurmak cihaz değişimi sayılır', line 84; 'anahtar kaybolur', line 235). On iOS, expo-secure-store data persists across uninstall when the app is reinstalled with the same bundle ID, so the software key can survive while the SQLite queue and sequence counter are deleted; if the app reuses that key, sequence numbers restart and collide with the server's unique (device, sequence) rule (line 612). On Android, Auto Backup is on by default in Expo and restores the database on install, while Keystore keys and expo-secure-store entries do not come back. App Attest keys do not survive reinstall, migration or backup restore either.

evidence.quote: On iOS: Data saved using expo-secure-store will persist across app uninstallations if the app is reinstalled with the same bundle ID.
Data is restored whenever the app is installed, whether from the Play Store, during device setup (when the system installs previously installed apps), or by running adb install.
Allows your user's app data to be automatically backed up to their Google Drive. ... Defaults to the Android default, which is `true`.
The keys that you generate remain valid through regular app updates, but don't survive app reinstallation, device migration, or restoration of a device from a backup.

findings.recommendation_tr: Android'de uygulama yedeğini kapatırım (allowBackup: false). Uygulama her açılışta yerel veritabanıyla telefondaki anahtarın birbirini tuttuğunu kontrol eder: veritabanı yoksa anahtar zincirinde kalan eski anahtarı siler; anahtar yoksa ya da tutmuyorsa cihaz değişimi akışını başlatır. Yedekten dönen imzalı bekleyen kayıtlar silinmez, cihaz değişimi kararına eklenir. Böylece yeniden kurulum gerçekten cihaz değişimi olur ve sıra numaraları çakışmaz.

findings.finding: Over-the-air updates are reversible (line 507), and expo-updates can also fall back to the bundle embedded in the binary ('emergency launch'). In both cases older JS can run against a local database that newer JS already migrated. The server has an expand-then-contract rule (line 583); the phone database has none, so a renamed or dropped column could crash the check-in path after a rollback.

evidence.quote: In very rare cases, it's possible that expo-updates may need to fall back to the update that's embedded in the app binary, even after newer updates have been downloaded and run (an "emergency launch").
instructs the client to run the update embedded in the build.

findings.recommendation_tr: Telefon veritabanı da yalnız ekleyerek değişir: tablo ve sütun eklenir, silinmez, adı değişmez. Yerel veritabanını değiştiren bir değişiklik uzaktan güncellemeyle gönderilmez, yeni sürümle gelir. Eski kod kendisinden yeni bir veritabanı görürse göç yapmadan çalışmaya devam eder.

findings.plan_quote: Gönderme kuyruğunda her kaydın kimliği, sıra numarası
findings.finding: Line 172 puts the instructor's head count under 'Derste, internet olmasa da', and early close and duration changes also happen in class (line 98). The queue is described only for student attendance records, while the student's problem report (line 145) and the app event log (line 151) are writes too. Without one shared queue these offline writes have no defined path, signature, trusted time or retry rule; early close in particular needs trusted time to decide which records count.

evidence.quote: When you have an object you want to write, insert it into a queue. When the app gets back online, drain the queue with exponential backoff.

findings.recommendation_tr: Kuyruğu telefondan yapılan bütün yazma işlemleri için ortak yazarım: öğrencinin yoklaması ve sorun bildirimi, hocanın kafa sayısı, erken kapatma, süre değişikliği, elle ekleme ve makbuz okutma aynı imza, saat belgesi ve yeniden deneme kuralıyla gider. findings.plan_quote: Program ve listeler "şu sürümden beri değişenler" diye çekilir; telefonun saati kullanılmaz.
findings.finding: Delta pulls need a defined reset path. If the server cannot serve a phone's cursor (deletion markers cleaned up, a pgBackRest restore to an earlier point leaving the phone's cursor ahead of the server, or a schema change), the phone silently keeps stale schedules and lists. Google's incremental sync protocol defines exactly this case.

evidence.quote: Sometimes sync tokens are invalidated by the server, for various reasons including token expiration or changes in related ACLs. In such cases, the server will respond to an incremental request with a response code 410. This should trigger a full wipe of the client's store and a new full sync.

findings.plan_quote: Android en sık 15 dakikada bir dener, iPhone'da zamanı sistem seçer.
findings.finding: Accurate but loose. Expo's iOS implementation submits a BGProcessingTaskRequest (requiresNetworkConnectivity = true), and Apple runs processing tasks only when the device is idle, so on iPhone background sending is mainly an idle, often overnight fallback. On Android 15 minutes is the floor, Expo's default minimumInterval is 12 hours, and standby buckets throttle rarely used apps. If a background send ever needs a keychain item stored with expo-secure-store's default WHEN_UNLOCKED, it cannot read it on a locked phone.

evidence.quote: Processing tasks run only when the device is idle. The system terminates any background processing tasks running when the user starts using the device.
let request = BGProcessingTaskRequest(identifier: ...) request.requiresNetworkConnectivity = true
Defaults to once every 12 hours (The minimum interval is 15 minutes)
Restricted | Once per day for up to 10 minutes
WHEN_UNLOCKED: The data in the keychain item can be accessed only while the device is unlocked by the user.

findings.recommendation_tr: Cümleyi şöyle netleştiririm: Android'de arka plan denemesi en sık 15 dakikada bir olur (bu değeri ayarda açıkça veririm, varsayılanı 12 saat) ve az kullanılan uygulamada sistem bunu seyrekleştirir; iPhone'da yalnız telefon boştayken, çoğunlukla gece çalışır. Arka plan gönderimi yalnız önceden imzalanmış kayıtları gönderir, kilitli telefonda anahtar zincirinden bir şey okumaz.

findings.finding: The receipt promises the record is stored. Expo's docs advise WAL mode; in WAL, SQLite is durable only with synchronous=FULL (the compile default, not overridden in expo-sqlite's iOS build flags). With synchronous=NORMAL, which performance guides often suggest for WAL, the last commit can roll back after a power loss or OS crash. Writes are a few per day, so FULL costs nothing.

evidence.quote: A transaction committed in WAL mode with synchronous=NORMAL might roll back following a power loss or system crash.
Enable WAL journal mode when you create a new database to improve performance in general.

findings.recommendation_tr: Yerel veritabanında WAL açılırsa synchronous ayarı FULL kalır, NORMAL'e düşürülmez. 'Telefonda kayıtlı' makbuzu yalnız yazma işlemi tamamlandıktan sonra gösterilir.

evidence.quote: include demo account info (and turn on your back-end service!) if your app includes a login. If you are unable to provide a demo account due to legal or security obligations, you may include a built-in demo mode in lieu of a demo account with prior approval by Apple.

Expo's own answer is the hosted EAS Observe service, which the plan's no-third-party rule excludes.

evidence.quote: You can export a nested ErrorBoundary component from any route to intercept and format component-level errors using React Error Boundaries

compactness_notes: Phase 1 phone native modules the plan implies: expo core; expo-router (required peers react-native-screens, react-native-safe-area-context, expo-linking, expo-constants; its npm dependencies also pull @expo/ui, expo-glass-effect, expo-symbols); expo-sqlite; expo-secure-store; @expo/app-integrity (alpha); own local module; expo-background-task plus its dependency expo-task-manager; expo-notifications (its Android build.gradle always includes com.google.firebase:firebase-messaging 25.0.1, even for local-only use); expo-updates; expo-network (already on Better Auth's Expo install line, so using it for the 'internet gelince' trigger adds nothing). expo-device is not needed: the plan rejects its uptime call and it only appears as a source link. Removable without real loss: on the phone drizzle-orm, drizzle-kit config, babel-plugin-inline-import and the babel/Metro edits (F04), and @tanstack/react-query (F03); both stay on server/panel. Additions from my findings: none (allowBackup is one app-config line; timeouts, Retry-After, cursor reset, shared queue and add-only local schema are code rules). Net on the phone package.json: minus 4 packages, minus 2 build-config edits, zero added. No lighter maintained local-notification library exists (@notifee/react-native last published 2024-12-20). Replacing Expo Router with bare React Navigation 7.5 would drop a few native packages but leaves Expo's default path; not recommended. Main app-size drivers: RN/Hermes core, expo-updates, the SQLite copy bundled by expo-sqlite, Firebase Messaging on Android; Phase 2 adds ML Kit (about 2.4 MB per plan). Arithmetic note: StatCounter sums were added by hand (no scripts allowed); raw components are in checked_ok for re-check.
open_questions: Does the send endpoint authenticate only by the record signatures, or does it also need a session or device token read from the keychain? If the latter, background sends on a locked iPhone will fail (F07).

Is the instructor's head count, early close and manual add meant to work offline in class (line 172 says yes)? If so, the shared queue in F12 is required, including trusted time on the instructor's phone.

Will the phone compute warning levels itself with packages/core to raise the local 'hak uyarısı', or only display levels computed by the server? This decides whether core must run identically under Hermes (F17).
Should the plan name SDK 58 now (stable expected right after React Native 0.88, currently rc.3) or keep 'newest stable SDK when phone work starts' wording (F01)?
How will the software key be stored on iOS (fixed keychain alias)? This decides whether a reinstall silently reuses it and restarts sequence numbers (F10).
